issues: B asserts 'non-decreasing', which looks stronger than A's 'monotonic' (either direction). The gap closes under the hypothesis. If f is non-increasing and satisfies 2f(x) ≤ f(x+h)+f(x+2h), then both f(x+h) ≤ f(x) and f(x+2h) ≤ f(x), so the sum is at most 2f(x). This forces f(x+h) = f(x) for all h > 0, so f is constant, hence also non-decreasing. So for functions satisfying the hypothesis, 'monotonic' and 'non-decreasing' are equivalent.
Quantifiers match: all f, all real x, all h > 0, with no regularity assumptions, as in A.
B implies A-YES directly; the equivalence above shows the extra strength in B is only apparent.

faithfulness.backtranslation: For every function f from the real numbers to the real numbers, suppose that for all real x and all real h > 0 we have 2f(x) ≤ f(x + h) + f(x + 2h). The claim is that every such f is non-decreasing on all of ℝ, meaning f(x) ≤ f(y) whenever x ≤ y. No continuity, measurability, or other regularity is assumed about f.
